pathway.title: IRON MOUNTAIN INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is stronger than the financial profile, and the gap between them is the credit. Global RIM Business produced 71.71% of nine-month revenue, storage rental was 56.73% of revenue, no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue and storage contracts run one to five years, so the cash base is recurring and diversified. Against that, net debt of 6.87x reported EBITDA and cash interest cover of 2.83x mean that the franchise's stability is already largely spent servicing debt: cash interest took 31.68% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Basis: calculation CAL-42; calculation CAL-44; calculation CAL-23; calculation CAL-7; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Deleveraging is real but earnings-led, and it overstates the operating gain. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell 1.01x in nine months while carrying-value debt rose USD 1,540.24 million and last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose USD 524.13 million; on Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back items that did not recur, net leverage eased only 0.16x to 6.16x. The improvement therefore reflects earnings already delivered, not debt repaid, and the dividend declared on 5 November 2026 is not reflected in these ratios, its pro forma effect on net debt not being established. Basis: calculation CAL-5; calculation CAL-6; calculation CAL-10; calculation CAL-11; calculation CAL-3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The cash shortfall is a growth choice, not an operating failure, which is the best argument that the credit can stabilise. In the nine months to 30 September 2026 operating cash flow less accrual-basis recurring capital expenditure was USD 1,085.34 million, and after dividends paid of USD 790.00 million it was still USD 295.34 million, so maintenance and the payout were self-funded; growth investment was 93.07% of capital spending and is what pushes free cash flow after capital expenditure to a shortfall of USD 536.82 million over the last twelve months. The weakness is that the dividend per share was raised 14.93% on 5 November 2026 while growth spending continues, which erodes that surplus. Basis: calculation CAL-18; calculation CAL-19; calculation CAL-20; calculation CAL-9; calculation CAL-51; calculation CAL-52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but rests on the revolver and open markets. Cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 2,406.38 million covered debt due within twelve months of USD 1,232.90 million 1.95x, and the company priced EUR 1,200.0 million of notes in 2025 and USD 1,500.0 million in 2026 at par; however, 14.08% of year-end 2025 principal falls due in 2027, the quarterly report prints no schedule after the 2026 refinancings, and revolver availability depends on a leverage test. Basis: calculation CAL-12; calculation CAL-13; calculation CAL-14; calculation CAL-15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 82–83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Rates and structure add pressure that the headline leverage hides. At least 24.86% of principal is floating-rate and swaps cover only USD 770.0 million of it after notional fell from USD 1,349.0 million at the end of 2025, so a 1% rise in rates would cost about USD 37.29 million a year, or 4.08% of cash interest; and the parent notes sit behind secured project loans, two partner-funded joint ventures that brought USD 124.70 million of noncontrolling interests and redeemable interests of USD 62,186 thousand with put options, so parent creditors rank behind more claims than net debt shows. Basis: calculation CAL-32; calculation CAL-34; calculation CAL-35; calculation CAL-53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Outlook is positive but the momentum in guidance is fading. Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised at all three releases, by USD 45.0 million, USD 15.0 million and USD 3.0 million at the midpoint, and the midpoint implies 15.11% growth over FY2025 and a fourth quarter 4.30% above the third; the small latest raise suggests management sees little further upside in 2026. Basis: calculation CAL-25; calculation CAL-26; calculation CAL-27; calculation CAL-28; calculation CAL-30; EX-99.1_2026-04-30_q12026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_final-q22026earningspres.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelea.htm.jsonl, page 2

The primary downside path is a data center slowdown that leaves debt-funded capacity idle, and arithmetic shows how little it takes to reverse the gain. A 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA with net debt unchanged would lift net debt over reported EBITDA to 7.63x and cut cover to 2.55x, close to the year-end 2025 levels of 7.88x and 2.50x; the company's own goodwill tests use a 10% cash flow reduction as their sensitivity step. Basis: calculation CAL-37; calculation CAL-38; calculation CAL-2; calculation CAL-8; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; Financial foundation (CP-1)

runs.text: Strength one: the records franchise is a durable, diversified cash source. Global RIM Business produced 71.71% of nine-month revenue at a segment Adjusted EBITDA margin of 43.75%, storage contracts run one to five years with steady volumes, and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, so cash flow is recurring and not concentrated. Creditors can rely on it to cover interest and maintenance spending even if growth slows. Basis: calculation CAL-42; calculation CAL-47; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength two: data centers are lifting EBITDA on long leases. Global Data Center Business revenue grew 39.61% in nine months at a segment margin of 53.60%, supplied 50.44% of the rise in reportable-segment Adjusted EBITDA, and leases average 10.3 years to expiry, so contracted rent underwrites the project loans that fund construction. Basis: calculation CAL-45; calculation CAL-46; calculation CAL-41; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength three: access to capital markets has been demonstrated. The company issued EUR 1,200.0 million of notes due 2034 and USD 1,500.0 million of notes due 2035 at par, extended its receivables programme to 2029 and held cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 2,406.38 million, so refinancing risk in the next year is lower than the debt due within a year of USD 1,232.90 million implies. Basis: calculation CAL-12; calculation CAL-14; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 82–83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength four: covenants leave room and carry no rating trigger. Covenant leverage of 4.8x is 2.2x inside its 7.0x maximum and fixed charge coverage of 2.5x is 1.0x above its 1.5x minimum, and a downgrade alone would not trigger a default. Basis: calculation CAL-54; calculation CAL-55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

Strength five: maintenance spending and the dividend are self-funded. Operating cash flow less recurring capital expenditure left USD 295.34 million after dividends in the nine months, so the borrowing need arises from growth investment that the company can slow. Basis: calculation CAL-19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7

Weakness one: leverage is high and falling only through earnings. Net debt is 6.87x reported EBITDA, down 1.01x in nine months while debt rose USD 1,540.24 million, so a stall in EBITDA growth would stop the improvement and the dividend declared on 5 November 2026 is not reflected, its pro forma effect on net debt not being established. Basis: calculation CAL-1; calculation CAL-5; calculation CAL-10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness two: free cash flow is negative and cover is thin. The last twelve months left a shortfall of USD 536.82 million after capital expenditure and before dividends, and reported EBITDA covered cash interest only 2.83x, so the build and payout depend on external funding. Basis: calculation CAL-9; calculation CAL-7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness three: parent creditors rank behind secured and partner claims. Project loans are secured on the data center subsidiaries, partners hold USD 124.70 million of noncontrolling interests, redeemable interests of USD 62,186 thousand carry put options, and the parent notes are effectively subordinated to secured debt and structurally subordinated to non-guarantor subsidiaries. Basis: calculation CAL-53; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness four: refinancing and rate exposure sit ahead. 14.08% of year-end 2025 principal falls due in 2027, at least 24.86% of principal is floating-rate with swaps covering only USD 770.0 million, and a 1% rate rise would cost about USD 37.29 million a year. Basis: calculation CAL-15; calculation CAL-32; calculation CAL-34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness five: data center execution and service volatility add earnings risk. Data centers took 79.79% of 2025 capital spend against 11.64% of revenue, 27.24% of annualized data center rent expires in 2026 to 2028, tenant concentration is not disclosed, and the asset lifecycle management unit's goodwill is the auditor's critical audit matter. Basis: calculation CAL-48; calculation CAL-49; calculation CAL-50; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No sponsor buyout or change of control is described in the seven documents, and the latest acquisition with a disclosed price is Regency Technologies in January 2024, so there is no entry multiple or sources and uses to report for the period. The transactions that matter to creditors are financings, partner joint ventures, one finance lease and a small run of acquisitions. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 133–134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Source readiness (CP-0)

New debt has been long-dated, with senior notes at the parent and secured project loans beside them. In September 2025 the company issued EUR 1,200.0 million of 4.75% senior notes due 2034 at par, and on 26 June 2026 it issued USD 1,500.0 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2035 at par, using net proceeds of USD 1,481.8 million to repay part of the revolving credit facility and for general corporate purposes. In January 2026 mortgage and mezzanine loans of USD 433.0 million due 2031 on the Virginia 3 data center replaced loans due in 2026, so the notes and the Virginia 3 loans together closed USD 1,933.00 million of term debt in 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation CAL-44

Other 2026 actions added capacity and extended maturities. The receivables securitisation programme was raised from USD 400.0 million to USD 450.0 million and extended from July 2027 to July 2029, with USD 408.0 million drawn at 30 September 2026. A new Virginia 9 credit agreement allows borrowing of up to USD 298.0 million at a margin of 3.00% over SOFR until June 2029, with USD 138.6 million drawn at the same date, and two joint ventures with partners added USD 124.70 million of noncontrolling interests. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation CAL-43

Two items outside debt matter for cash. A 31-year data center finance lease signed in February 2026, with undiscounted minimum payments of about USD 223.4 million, is expected to start in the fourth quarter of 2026. On 5 November 2026, after the balance sheet date, the board declared a quarterly dividend 14.93% above the previous one, payable in January 2027. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation CAL-40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for IRON MOUNTAIN INC (irm) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the consolidated statements of Iron Mountain Incorporated for FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, with debt, liquidity, leverage and cash interest cover drawn from the seven supplied documents; no credit recommendation is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high but easing: net debt was 6.87x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, down from 7.88x at the end of 2025, so creditors depend on continued EBITDA growth to keep refinancing risk contained. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 2.83x over the same twelve months, or 3.16x on the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was cash of USD 188.16 million plus USD 2.22 billion of undrawn revolver, against USD 1.23 billion of debt due within a year, while capital spending still exceeds operating cash flow. The quarterly reports print no year-by-year maturity schedule, so the wall at that date is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt over last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell from 7.88x at the end of 2025 to 6.87x at 30 September 2026. The improvement came from EBITDA growth, not repayment: carrying-value debt rose by USD 1,540.243 million over the nine months while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 524.128 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Part of the reported gain is relief from items that did not recur: the issuer booked USD 152.432 million of restructuring and other transformation in the first nine months of 2025 and prints a dash for it in 2026, and other expense (income), net fell from USD 106.379 million to USD 32.910 million. On the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds those items back, net leverage eased by only 0.16x against 1.01x on reported EBITDA, so the headline deleveraging overstates the operating improvement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is operating momentum and covenant room: Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 660.379 million in the third quarter of 2025 to USD 747.958 million in the third quarter of 2026, and the leverage ratio the issuer reports under its Credit Agreement sits inside its limit. That reading would win if reported EBITDA keeps converging on Adjusted EBITDA as restructuring ends, narrowing the gap from USD 508.992 million in FY2025 to USD 299.106 million in the last twelve months. Interest cover moved the same way, from 2.50x to 2.83x on reported EBITDA, but remains thin for a borrower whose capital spending exceeds its operating cash flow.

fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-39; calculation CAL-40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure exceeds operating cash flow, so growth is funded externally. In FY2025 operating cash flow of USD 1,339.999 million fell USD 931.629 million short of capital expenditure of USD 2,271.628 million, before dividends of USD 919.388 million. Over the last twelve months to 30 September 2026 the shortfall narrowed to USD 536.818 million, and the issuer expects total capital expenditure of about USD 2,200.0 million in 2026, of which about USD 2,050.0 million is growth investment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The mechanism is data center construction financed by project debt, noncontrolling-interest equity (USD 95.168 million contributed in the nine months to 30 September 2026) and the revolver, which keeps total debt rising even as the ratio falls. The credit implication is that leverage stays sensitive to how fast leased capacity converts to EBITDA and to the cost and availability of refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 188.160 million and undrawn revolver availability of USD 2,218.218 million at 30 September 2026 compare with debt due within twelve months of USD 1,232.903 million, up from USD 216.074 million at the year end. The annual report lists USD 2,330.763 million due in 2027 and USD 1,663.693 million in 2028 at the year end, so the near-term wall is front-loaded and the 2027 notes are among the next refinancing tests; the quarterly report does not itemise the current portion or print a schedule at 30 September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The availability figure is the issuer's maximum under its Credit Agreement tests and the compliance statement in the quarterly report applies to those tests, so liquidity depends on the revolver staying available as leverage moves. The filings state that the covenants contain no rating trigger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer states only an adjusted measure, and the covenant ratios use further definitions that are not directly comparable with either. Debt is carrying value; principal is USD 124.224 million higher at 30 September 2026. Operating lease liabilities of USD 2,518.768 million sit outside debt, while financing lease liabilities are inside it. Deferred revenue of USD 378.117 million is non-debt funding float, down from USD 402.091 million at the year end.

fields.value: Each calculation below shows its inputs; ratios, last-twelve-months derivations and the free cash flow figures are worked in the registers above with their operands, and every figure is in the unit stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt maturities by year at 2026-09-30: no quarterly report prints a schedule, so the ladder is drawn at 2025-12-31, before the Virginia 3 refinancing, the securitization amendment and the 2035 notes; this restricts the maturity wall to the year-end view and the printed current portion at 2026-09-30. Severity: High. Action: obtain the issuer's schedule at the latest date or derive it, labelled derived, from instrument principal and stated maturities.

fields.value: - Debt stack: Real Estate Mortgages, Financing Lease Liabilities and Other (carrying USD 818.241 million) is left out of the stack because no source states the rank of the pool, and the stack therefore adds to less than total debt; this restricts the cumulative leverage in the stack to the instruments whose rank is stated. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the component ranking and security.

fields.value: - Lease payments and purchase commitments by year at 2026-09-30: the quarterly reports print lease balances and one new finance lease but no payment schedule; the annual report schedule is at 2025-12-31. This restricts claims outside debt to year-end schedules and balances at the latest date. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the schedule at the latest date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance for IRON MOUNTAIN INC (irm) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway, a public-company case reported in USD. Scope: what the business is, who owns and governs it, how it earns money, which dated transactions shape it and where the seven supplied documents fall short; no transaction, sponsor deal or instrument recommendation is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Iron Mountain is a listed real estate investment trust with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the filings, so creditor risk comes from management's debt-funded data center build and rising dividend, not from sponsor extraction. Creditors get disclosure and covenants rather than control: the board sets dividends at its sole discretion, and the charter caps any one holder at 9.8% of the capital stock, subject to exceptions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating base is steadier than the capital plan: storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, while data centers produced 50.44% of the nine-month rise in reportable-segment Adjusted EBITDA on 13.28% of revenue. That growth outruns internal cash: operating cash flow covered 69.81% of capital spending in the nine months to 30 September 2026, before USD 790.00 million of dividends, and net new senior-note proceeds of USD 1,485.00 million covered the USD 1,310.57 million left after dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CAL-28; calculation CAL-21; calculation CAL-35; calculation CAL-37; calculation CAL-38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor stands behind the credit and none is named above it, so the creditor-adverse behaviours to test are the board's own funding and payout choices, not a sponsor's leakage. The registrant is the top company of its own group, no preferred shares are in issue, and the filings name neither a parent nor a controlling holder; the holder list itself sits in a proxy statement that is not among the supplied documents, so control is not established beyond the charter cap. Creditors have no equity cure or parent support to rely on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 37; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is sound and governance is conventional for a listed company, which supports monitoring but does not bind management. Both the annual statements and internal control carry unqualified audit opinions, each quarterly report is dated the same day as the matching earnings release, eleven directors signed the annual report including the chief executive, and the board oversees enterprise risk through a risk and safety committee. Director independence, the chair's role and director shareholdings are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dividend policy is the clearest creditor-adverse behaviour, because payouts rise while investment outruns operating cash flow. The quarterly dividend per share rose 10.06% in November 2025 and 14.93% in November 2026; in the nine months to 30 September 2026 the company paid USD 790.00 million of dividends while operating cash flow of USD 1,203.63 million covered 69.81% of capital spending of USD 1,724.21 million, and net senior-note proceeds of USD 1,485.00 million filled the gap. The real estate investment trust payout rule and a public pledge to grow dividends make the payout hard to cut, so it competes with debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-34; calculation CAL-32; calculation CAL-33; calculation CAL-35; calculation CAL-38; calculation CAL-39; calculation CAL-40; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 152; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth capital is increasingly raised against single assets and with partners, which puts those lenders ahead of parent creditors on the assets concerned and shares the cash flows of the ventures with partners. At least four data center loans are secured on project subsidiaries' property or equity, including a new facility of up to USD 298.0 million signed in June 2026, and two partner-funded joint ventures added USD 124.70 million of noncontrolling interests. The parent notes are guaranteed only by U.S. subsidiaries holding the substantial majority of U.S. operations and are effectively subordinated to secured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The records base is durable and the data center book is long-dated, but data center rent rolls over faster than the headline lease length suggests. Contracted storage runs one to five years with steady volumes, no customer is above about 3% of revenue, and data center leases average 10.3 years to expiry; even so, 27.24% of annualized data center rent expires in 2026 to 2028, and service growth in records and tape work is held back as stored records become less active.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition appetite is modest and revolver-funded, but the Regency Technologies earn-out is an identifiable cash call. Cash paid for acquisitions was USD 8.03 million in the nine months to 30 September 2026 against USD 101.63 million a year earlier, while the deferred purchase obligations, mostly that earn-out, rose to USD 210.19 million; an earn-out of up to USD 200.0 million would be payable in 2027 if earned. Redeemable noncontrolling interests of USD 62,186 thousand also carry put options on terms the documents do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall sponsor and governance risk reads as medium. Transparent reporting, no sponsor extraction, no liability management in the documents and covenant compliance sit against a debt-funded build, a rising payout, ring-fenced project debt and an ownership base the supplied documents cannot confirm.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium reading is on the supportive side. Covenant ratios were well inside their limits at 30 September 2026 (net total lease adjusted leverage of 4.8x against a maximum of 7.0x, a headroom of 2.2x, and fixed charge coverage of 2.5x against a minimum of 1.5x, a headroom of 1.0x), the debt terms carry no rating trigger, no shares were repurchased in the latest quarter, maturities were extended through new notes, a refinanced project loan and a longer receivables programme with no waiver or covenant relief described, and the documents describe no priming, exchange offer or non-pro-rata transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against that, the dividend and the build could be more adverse than stated if the debt documents leave room for larger distributions, because the filings summarise covenants but do not show baskets. The view would turn adverse if the proxy statement showed a holder with board or veto rights, if the board funded a special distribution or buyback with debt while leverage sat near its limits, or if capital spending stayed above operating cash flow after leasing slowed. It would turn favourable if operating cash flow covered capital spending and dividends as the build tapers, or if executed debt documents showed tight restricted-payment limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Holder names, holder percentages and board independence are not in the supplied documents, so the conclusion that no holder controls the company rests on the charter cap and on the absence of any named holder, and stays provisional until a holder list is seen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The documents give no tenant-level detail for data centers beyond a statement that five of the largest hyperscalers are customers, so the durability of data center cash flow cannot be tested for tenant concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 acquisitions are not named or priced, so the conclusion on acquisition appetite rests on cash paid and goodwill acquired alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed debt documents are not supplied, so whether dividend and investment baskets leave room for a larger distribution is not established and the dividend conclusion rests on observed payments rather than on legal capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor buyout or change of control is described in the seven documents, and the latest acquisition with a disclosed price is Regency Technologies in January 2024, so there is no entry multiple or sources and uses to report for the period. The transactions that matter to creditors are financings, partner joint ventures, one finance lease and a small run of acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 133–134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt has been long-dated, with senior notes at the parent and secured project loans beside them. In September 2025 the company issued EUR 1,200.0 million of 4.75% senior notes due 2034 at par, and on 26 June 2026 it issued USD 1,500.0 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2035 at par, using net proceeds of USD 1,481.8 million to repay part of the revolving credit facility and for general corporate purposes. In January 2026 mortgage and mezzanine loans of USD 433.0 million due 2031 on the Virginia 3 data center replaced loans due in 2026, so the notes and the Virginia 3 loans together closed USD 1,933.00 million of term debt in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other 2026 actions added capacity and extended maturities. The receivables securitisation programme was raised from USD 400.0 million to USD 450.0 million and extended from July 2027 to July 2029, with USD 408.0 million drawn at 30 September 2026. A new Virginia 9 credit agreement allows borrowing of up to USD 298.0 million at a margin of 3.00% over SOFR until June 2029, with USD 138.6 million drawn at the same date, and two joint ventures with partners added USD 124.70 million of noncontrolling interests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two items outside debt matter for cash. A 31-year data center finance lease signed in February 2026, with undiscounted minimum payments of about USD 223.4 million, is expected to start in the fourth quarter of 2026. On 5 November 2026, after the balance sheet date, the board declared a quarterly dividend 14.93% above the previous one, payable in January 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registers below hold the full detail behind the findings; figures are as printed or as worked in the calculations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module Status: Ready with Limitations. The business, transaction and governance evidence is sufficient for the registers below; holder, board independence and executed debt-document detail are missing.

fields.value: The risk level is driven by a payout that grows while capital spending exceeds operating cash flow and by project-level debt that ranks ahead of the notes, because both reduce the cash and assets available to parent creditors, which implies that refinancing and recovery depend on continued earnings growth. Countervailing evidence is covenant headroom, no rating trigger, timely and assured reporting, and the absence of any sponsor extraction or liability management in the documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for IRON MOUNTAIN INC (irm) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway, a public-company case reported in USD. Scope: the overall credit profile, its strongest support, its weakest dimension and its primary downside path, built from the seven supplied documents and the three earlier analyses; no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Iron Mountain's fundamental credit is adequate but leverage-dependent: a contracted, diversified records base and a growing data center book support cash flow, yet net debt of 6.87x reported EBITDA, thin interest cover and negative free cash flow make credit quality depend on EBITDA outgrowing debt. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 7.88x at the end of 2025 to 6.87x at 30 September 2026 because earnings grew while debt rose; the dividend declared on 5 November 2026 is not reflected, and its pro forma effect on net debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-1; calculation CAL-2; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is the records franchise, which is contracted, diversified and still produces most revenue, while data centers now supply about half of the growth in segment EBITDA. The primary downside is a slower data center build-out: spending is committed ahead of rent, so a stall would hold leverage near its current level while USD 1,232.90 million of debt due within a year and the 2027 maturities come due.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-41; calculation CAL-42; calculation CAL-14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is stronger than the financial profile, and the gap between them is the credit. Global RIM Business produced 71.71% of nine-month revenue, storage rental was 56.73% of revenue, no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue and storage contracts run one to five years, so the cash base is recurring and diversified. Against that, net debt of 6.87x reported EBITDA and cash interest cover of 2.83x mean that the franchise's stability is already largely spent servicing debt: cash interest took 31.68% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging is real but earnings-led, and it overstates the operating gain. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell 1.01x in nine months while carrying-value debt rose USD 1,540.24 million and last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose USD 524.13 million; on Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back items that did not recur, net leverage eased only 0.16x to 6.16x. The improvement therefore reflects earnings already delivered, not debt repaid, and the dividend declared on 5 November 2026 is not reflected in these ratios, its pro forma effect on net debt not being established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-5; calculation CAL-6; calculation CAL-10; calculation CAL-11; calculation CAL-3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cash shortfall is a growth choice, not an operating failure, which is the best argument that the credit can stabilise. In the nine months to 30 September 2026 operating cash flow less accrual-basis recurring capital expenditure was USD 1,085.34 million, and after dividends paid of USD 790.00 million it was still USD 295.34 million, so maintenance and the payout were self-funded; growth investment was 93.07% of capital spending and is what pushes free cash flow after capital expenditure to a shortfall of USD 536.82 million over the last twelve months. The weakness is that the dividend per share was raised 14.93% on 5 November 2026 while growth spending continues, which erodes that surplus.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but rests on the revolver and open markets. Cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 2,406.38 million covered debt due within twelve months of USD 1,232.90 million 1.95x, and the company priced EUR 1,200.0 million of notes in 2025 and USD 1,500.0 million in 2026 at par; however, 14.08% of year-end 2025 principal falls due in 2027, the quarterly report prints no schedule after the 2026 refinancings, and revolver availability depends on a leverage test.

fields.value: Rates and structure add pressure that the headline leverage hides. At least 24.86% of principal is floating-rate and swaps cover only USD 770.0 million of it after notional fell from USD 1,349.0 million at the end of 2025, so a 1% rise in rates would cost about USD 37.29 million a year, or 4.08% of cash interest; and the parent notes sit behind secured project loans, two partner-funded joint ventures that brought USD 124.70 million of noncontrolling interests and redeemable interests of USD 62,186 thousand with put options, so parent creditors rank behind more claims than net debt shows.

fields.value: Outlook is positive but the momentum in guidance is fading. Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised at all three releases, by USD 45.0 million, USD 15.0 million and USD 3.0 million at the midpoint, and the midpoint implies 15.11% growth over FY2025 and a fourth quarter 4.30% above the third; the small latest raise suggests management sees little further upside in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a data center slowdown that leaves debt-funded capacity idle, and arithmetic shows how little it takes to reverse the gain. A 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA with net debt unchanged would lift net debt over reported EBITDA to 7.63x and cut cover to 2.55x, close to the year-end 2025 levels of 7.88x and 2.50x; the company's own goodwill tests use a 10% cash flow reduction as their sensitivity step.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious reading is that the shortfall is discretionary and the business is outgrowing its debt: growth investment is 93.07% of capital spending, operating cash flow covers maintenance and the dividend with USD 295.34 million to spare, covenant leverage of 4.8x sits 2.2x inside its 7.0x maximum and fixed charge coverage of 2.5x sits 1.0x above its 1.5x minimum, the debt terms carry no rating trigger, and the company has extended maturities at par in both bond markets. That reading would win if growth spending slowed while Adjusted EBITDA kept rising and the 2027 maturities were refinanced without a rise in cost.

The guidance range for 2026 Adjusted EBITDA starts at USD 2,948 million, and a full-year result below it would be the first sign that growth is not covering the cost of the build.

fields.value: Strength one: the records franchise is a durable, diversified cash source. Global RIM Business produced 71.71% of nine-month revenue at a segment Adjusted EBITDA margin of 43.75%, storage contracts run one to five years with steady volumes, and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, so cash flow is recurring and not concentrated. Creditors can rely on it to cover interest and maintenance spending even if growth slows.

fields.value: Weakness five: data center execution and service volatility add earnings risk. Data centers took 79.79% of 2025 capital spend against 11.64% of revenue, 27.24% of annualized data center rent expires in 2026 to 2028, tenant concentration is not disclosed, and the asset lifecycle management unit's goodwill is the auditor's critical audit matter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Iron Mountain is a global information management group whose cash base is physical records storage and whose growth comes from data centers, digital solutions and asset lifecycle management. Global RIM Business produced 71.71% of nine-month 2026 revenue, Global Data Center Business 13.28% and Corporate and Other, which holds asset lifecycle management, 15.01%; storage rental was 56.73% of revenue and the United States 66.27% of FY2025 revenue, with other countries outside the United Kingdom and Canada 22.51%. The recurring, contracted rental base gives cash flow visibility and debt service capacity, while the service and asset lifecycle management lines add revenue that moves with activity and component prices.

fields.value: Credit-relevant history is acquisitive but modest: the Regency Technologies purchase in January 2024 carries an earn-out of up to USD 200.0 million payable in 2027 if earned, and Project Matterhorn, a transformation programme of about USD 574.4 million, ended in 2025 so restructuring cost no longer weighs on 2026 cash flow. The earn-out is a contingent call on liquidity in the same year as the USD 1,000.0 million of notes due in September 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Iron Mountain is a listed holding company with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named; the charter caps any holder at 9.8% and the board sets dividends in its sole discretion, so creditors depend on governance and covenants rather than on a sponsor. Sponsor and governance risk is medium in Business & governance: reporting is transparent and covenants have headroom, but the payout is growing, project debt is ring-fenced and the proxy statement that would confirm holders is not among the supplied documents. The indentures treat a leveraged recapitalization as outside the change-of-control repurchase right, so the change-of-control put gives noteholders no protection against a debt-funded recapitalization.

Detailed ranking is for the legal and structural analyses and is not concluded here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable in storage and data centers and cyclical or discretionary in service lines. Nine-month organic revenue growth was 15.6%, made up of storage rental at 11.6% and service at 21.3%; in Global RIM Business storage rental grew 5.4% organically on pricing with volume steady, while Global Data Center Business revenue grew 39.61% on lease commencements, pricing and power usage. Pricing power in records is therefore the base-business lever and carries the risk that price rises meet customer resistance as stored records become less active, whereas data center growth depends on leasing and energising capacity on schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Service revenue and asset lifecycle management add volatility: Corporate and Other service revenue rose 61.0% in nine months partly through acquisitions and component pricing, buyers of decommissioned components are concentrated in China, and commodity prices move paper and scrap-metal sales. The unit's goodwill sensitivity is modest, with fair value 93.7% above carrying value at 1 October 2025, which limits near-term impairment risk but does not protect cash flow from a price fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are resilient on the consolidated measure and uneven underneath. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.7% in the nine months against 36.9% a year earlier; cost of sales rose to 46.6% of revenue from 44.6% as product cost of sales in asset lifecycle management went from 7.5% to 11.3% of revenue, offset by selling, general and administrative expense falling to 18.9% from 20.9%. Global RIM Business margin slipped to 43.7% from 44.4% while Global Data Center Business margin rose to 53.60%, so mix toward data centers supports margin and mix toward asset lifecycle management dilutes it; labor at 16.2% and facilities at 16.6% of revenue are treated here as largely fixed in the short run, which gives operating leverage on the way up and on the way down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high and almost all of it is discretionary growth spending. Last-twelve-months operating cash flow converted 58.99% of Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest took 31.68%, and in nine months growth investment was 93.07% of capital spending, of which 84.56% went to data centers; 2026 capital expenditure guidance is about USD 2,200.0 million of which USD 2,050.0 million is growth. Capital spending is flexible to the extent leases are not already committed, so the shortfall of USD 536.82 million over the last twelve months can narrow quickly if the company chooses, but customers who have preleased space in data centers under construction limit how fast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-24; calculation CAL-23; calculation CAL-20; calculation CAL-21; calculation CAL-9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leases and claims outside debt add fixed obligations: operating lease liabilities of USD 2,518.77 million sit outside debt, level 3 deferred purchase obligations of USD 210.19 million and redeemable noncontrolling interests of USD 62,186 thousand carry cash claims, and a 31-year data center finance lease with undiscounted payments of about USD 223.4 million is due to start in the fourth quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-59; calculation CAL-60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive pressure is moderate in records and higher in data centers and asset lifecycle management. In records most competitors operate in one market or region, so Iron Mountain's global scale and chain-of-custody record are a barrier that supports pricing; in data centers it competes with many developers on power availability, security, location, connectivity and rent, and in asset lifecycle management it competes with hyperscalers and corporate clients that process their own assets. New entrants face high capital and power barriers in data centers and trust barriers in records, which protects existing cash flows but also means the company must keep spending to hold its position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes and buyers are the main sources of pressure on the base business: customers who adopt non-paper storage or retain records for less time shrink the physical volume and shift revenue from predictable storage to volatile service, and some large-customer contracts carry no limit on liability. Supplier power is real in data centers, where power, construction contractors and permits drive cost and timing, and in asset lifecycle management, where component buyers are concentrated; the credit consequence is cost and delay risk on the capacity that debt is funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest rates, currency and tax rules matter to credit; political and social factors do not appear to be primary drivers in the supplied documents. Floating-rate debt and thin cover make rate changes material, 22.51% of FY2025 revenue arises outside the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada with euro and sterling debt acting as a partial natural hedge, a 10% depreciation of functional currencies would reduce equity by USD 374.7 million, and the real estate investment trust rules require a 90% distribution of taxable income, while a 2026 change in the limit on assets held in taxable subsidiaries and the global minimum tax are not expected to have a material effect. Digitisation and artificial intelligence cut both ways: they reduce physical record activity but support digital solutions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-32; calculation CAL-57; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the contracted records base, long data center leases of 10.3 years on average and demonstrated market access; weaknesses are leverage of 6.87x reported EBITDA, a free cash flow shortfall of USD 536.82 million over the last twelve months and claims that rank ahead of parent noteholders. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are converting the data center development pipeline into leased rent and cross-selling, because only about 5% of customers buy from more than one business unit; threats that could weaken it are power and construction cost or delay, a faster shift away from physical records and higher refinancing cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-1; calculation CAL-9; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 28–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Taking the nine dimensions in turn, scale and market position is strong, competitive advantage is average to strong in records and average in data centers and asset lifecycle management, business diversification is average because customers are diversified but 71.71% of revenue comes from one segment, cost and capex flexibility is average because growth spending is discretionary but partly committed, and margin stability is average to strong because the consolidated margin moved only 20 bp. Free cash flow stability is weak because the last twelve months left a shortfall of USD 536.82 million after capital expenditure, ability to refinance is average because access has been shown but 2027 maturities and floating-rate debt remain, liquidity is average at 1.95x cover of debt due within a year, and financial policy and governance is average because reporting is transparent and covenants have headroom while the payout is growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-42; calculation CAL-9; calculation CAL-13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_irm-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are the records base, data center EBITDA growth and market access; the main constraints are leverage, negative free cash flow and ranking. The trend is improving, with net debt over reported EBITDA at 6.87x against 7.88x and cash interest cover at 2.83x against 2.50x, but the improvement came from earnings and not from lower debt. Key missing datapoints are the debt maturity schedule after the 2026 refinancings, tenant concentration in data centers, covenant definitions and a rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-1; calculation CAL-2; calculation CAL-7; calculation CAL-8; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is supportive: management guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to USD 2,948 million to USD 2,978 million, a midpoint 15.11% above FY2025, has signed new data center leases this year, and says additional capacity is due to be energized over the next 24 months. Those are management statements and the rise in guidance is flattening, with the latest increase at the midpoint only USD 3.0 million. Tailwinds are lease commencements, pricing in records and falling restructuring cost; headwinds are higher power and construction cost, a rising dividend, rate-sensitive refinancing and records that are becoming less active.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the credit depends on converting the development pipeline into leased, cash-generating capacity while holding leverage steady: 27.24% of annualized data center rent expires in 2026 to 2028, which gives repricing opportunity but also re-leasing risk, and the 2027 and 2028 note maturities must be refinanced at current market cost. The records base is expected by management to stay relatively consistent in volume, so its contribution is stable cash rather than growth.

fields.value: Basis: calculation CAL-50; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-K_2025-12-31_irm-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path starts with a delay or shortfall in data center leasing or energizing while construction commitments continue, and turns into a leverage and refinancing problem rather than an immediate liquidity one. Revenue growth in the data center segment, now 39.61%, would slow first; because facility costs and the debt service on completed capacity would continue while rent was delayed, the segment margin of 53.60% would fall, and service and asset lifecycle management revenue would add to the pressure if component prices or activity weakened. As an arithmetic sensitivity and not a forecast, a 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA with net debt and interest unchanged lifts net debt over reported EBITDA from 6.87x to 7.63x and cuts cash interest cover from 2.83x to 2.55x, close to the year-end 2025 levels of 7.88x and 2.50x, or to 6.84x and 2.84x on Adjusted EBITDA; a 1% rise in rates on uncovered floating-rate debt would add about USD 37.29 million of annual interest, 4.08% of cash interest, against the company's own year-end 2025 sensitivity of USD 41.9 million of net income for a 1% rise on 22.0% variable-rate debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within a year: cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 2,406.38 million covers debt due within twelve months of USD 1,232.90 million 1.95x, the growth budget of USD 2,050.0 million can be reduced, partners contributed USD 95.17 million of equity in nine months, and covenant leverage of 4.8x sits 2.2x inside its 7.0x maximum. The levers are limited by the real estate investment trust distribution rule, which makes the dividend hard to cut, by minor asset-sale proceeds of USD 11.03 million, and by revolver availability that depends on the leverage test, so the exposure is to leverage staying near its current level while about 14.08% of year-end 2025 principal needs refinancing in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Iron Mountain presents an adequate business profile supported by a contracted, diversified records base and long-dated data center leases, but credit quality is constrained by net debt of 6.87x reported EBITDA, a free cash flow shortfall of USD 536.82 million over the last twelve months and claims that rank ahead of parent noteholders. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because maintenance spending and the dividend are self-funded and covenants have headroom, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued EBITDA growth, the revolver and open bond markets, with about 14.08% of year-end 2025 principal due in 2027. The primary downside path is a data center slowdown that leaves debt-funded capacity idle while the payout keeps rising. Further analysis would require the maturity schedule after the 2026 refinancings, tenant concentration, the executed debt documents and a rating, and the dividend declared on 5 November 2026 is not reflected in the leverage figures, its pro forma effect on net debt not being established. The top risk is leverage that stays near its current level because EBITDA growth stalls.
